name: AMD 8xMI355X, MLPerf Inference v6.1 Offline: Llama 2 70B on AMD's own node, aggregate output throughput
methodology: AGGREGATE. MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed division, Datacenter suite, Offline scenario, submitted by AMD itself on Supermicro AS-4126GS-NMR-LCC, 1 node, 8x AMD Instinct MI355X 288GB HBM3e. LOADS: batch size not a fixed published number (closed-loop Offline queue, submitter-chosen scheduler batching); binding conditions are min_duration 600000 ms, min_query_count 2000, early stopping satisfied: Yes. Model shape TOKENS_PER_SAMPLE 267.0. Framework per summary.csv: 'PyTorch 2.10.0+git8514f05, ROCm 7.2.2'; the LLM serving path for this submission is vLLM (the repo's other AMD v6.0/v6.1 records attribute MI355X Llama 2 70B runs to vLLM with matching vLLM version strings), so engine_id is recorded as vllm while noting the row itself names only PyTorch/ROCm. Samples per second 375.84. POWER: has_power=False, design_power_watts=null, no declared cap, no cooling configuration declared. OMITTED BY SOURCE: TP size, KV-cache dtype, concurrency, clock state.
notes: AMD's own v6.1 MI355X number lands within 2.6% of NVIDIA's DGX B300 on the same model and the same scenario (106517 vs 109277), despite B300 having 270GB against MI355X's 288GB. That near-tie is the most useful single fact in the v6.1 LLM set: on this model at FP4, an 8-GPU AMD node and an 8-GPU NVIDIA node are the same product. Do not upgrade this into a 'MI355X beats B300' claim - the 2.6% is well inside the spread between OEM implementations of the same GPU (Supermicro's MI355X node gives 102243, HPE's gives 102991, Oracle's gives 101553 for this exact scenario, a 1.4% band), and the FP4 formats are not even the same scheme (AMD mxfp4 vs NVIDIA nvfp4).
